name: Egmont National Park
note: National park (destination level): Te Papa-Kura-o-Taranaki, formerly Egmont National Park, around Taranaki Maunga.

name: New Plymouth
note: City (regional hub and base): the main city of Taranaki on the coast below the mountain.

name: Stratford
note: Town (gateway): inland town on the eastern slopes of the mountain, start of the Forgotten World Highway.

name: Hāwera
note: Town (South Taranaki hub): main service town at the south end of Surf Highway 45.

name: Ōpunake
note: Town (small surf town with galleries and studios) on Surf Highway 45.

name: Ōakura
note: Village (surf village with beach and cafés) on Surf Highway 45, south-west of New Plymouth.

name: Ōkato
note: Village (coastal village on Surf Highway 45) with a fish-and-chip takeaway and access to Lucy's Gully.

name: Pātea
note: Town (South Taranaki) with a museum, a sculpture and Pātea Beach.

name: Eltham
note: Town (inland dairy town) with a cheese store and access to Lake Rotokare.

name: Inglewood
note: Town (inland town on State Highway 3 between New Plymouth and Stratford), a route stop.

name: Waitara
note: Town (port town north of New Plymouth), listed in the region's cities.

name: Waverley
note: Town (small South Taranaki town) with a glass art studio.

name: Manaia
note: Town (small South Taranaki town on SH45) known for its bread factory; a stop per NZ Pocket Guide only.

name: Whangamōmona
note: Village (gateway settlement on the Forgotten World Highway): self-declared republic with a historic hotel; its draw is the journey beyond it and the Republic Day.

name: Tongapōrutu
note: Village (coastal settlement north of New Plymouth) and access point for Elephant Rock and Three Sisters.

name: Taranaki Maunga
note: Mountain (2,518 m stratovolcano, the park's central peak): the main attraction, with summit climbs and the surrounding tracks.

name: Pouākai Crossing
note: Track (one-day walk, 18.4 km, 7–9 hours) across the Pouākai range from North Taranaki to Mangorei Road; named by the tourism board as the premier one-day walk.

name: Pouākai Circuit
note: Track (multi-day circuit, 2–3 days) starting at North Egmont and passing the Pouākai range and tarns.

name: Pouākai Tarn
note: Lake (pair of alpine tarns on the Pouākai plateau) famous for mirror reflections of the mountain.

name: Pouākai Range
note: Mountain range (ridge on the park's north side) crossed by the Pouākai Crossing and Pouākai Circuit.

name: Ahukawakawa Swamp
note: Wetland (fragile swamp) crossed by the Pouākai Crossing, no mobile coverage.

name: Dieffenbach Cliffs
note: Cliffs (towering lava columns) seen from the Pouākai Crossing.

name: Taranaki Maunga Summit Climb
note: Track (8–12 hour climb to the summit area, the park's most challenging walk); the summit is sacred to tangata whenua.

name: Around the Mountain Circuit
note: Track (multi-day loop of the mountain on DOC's track network).

name: Dawson Falls
note: Waterfall (18 m waterfall over lava formations, known locally as Te Rere o Noke) with a 250 m track to its base.

name: Dawson Falls Visitor Centre
note: Visitor centre (DOC park information at Dawson Falls, not a spot in itself).

name: Dawson Falls Power Station
note: Heritage site (historic power station named by DOC as a place to discover).

name: Wilkies Pools
note: Natural lava plunge pools with views of the mountain, reached by an easy 1.9 km loop walk.

name: Goblin Forest
note: Forest (mossy goblin forest on the Kapuni Loop Track) reached from the Dawson Falls car park.

name: Curtis Falls Track
note: Track (DOC walking track to Curtis Falls in the park).

name: Kamahi Loop Track
note: Track (DOC loop walk through the park's forest).

name: Veronica Loop Track
note: Track (DOC loop walk in the park).

name: York Road Loop Track
note: Track (DOC loop walk in the park).

name: Track to Dawson Falls
note: Track (DOC walk from the Dawson Falls area).

name: Waimoku Track
note: Track (4–5 hour return walk through the Kaitake forest from Lucy's Gully).

name: Sefton Ridge Track
note: Track (2-hour loop from Lucy's Gully through the Kaitake Ranges).

name: Mangorei Track
note: Track (short two-hour one-way walk from Mangorei Road into the park, also the Pouākai Crossing finish).

name: Manganui Gorge Track
note: Track (walk to the 100 m Manganui Gorge suspension bridge, 49.5 m above the gorge floor, opened May 2024).

name: Manganui Ski Area
note: Ski field (small seasonal ski area on the mountain, open early June to mid-October).

name: Holly Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation on the Pouākai Crossing route, not a sight).

name: Pouākai Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation near the Pouākai Tarn, bookings essential), not a sight.

name: Syme Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation on the Panitahi and Syme Hut track), not a sight.

name: Kahui Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation), not a sight.

name: Maketawa Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation), not a sight.

name: Waiaua Gorge Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation), not a sight.

name: Waingongoro Hut
note: Hut (DOC overnight accommodation), not a sight.

name: The Camphouse

name: Ambury Monument
note: Memorial (monument and bluff at North Egmont named after Arthur Ambury, who died in 1918).

name: North Taranaki Visitor Centre
note: Visitor centre (DOC, at North Egmont; under construction until December 2026 per the tourism board), not a spot.

name: Fanthams Peak
note: Peak (secondary peak of the mountain, on the route from Dawson Falls).

name: Kaitake Range

name: Stony River Walkway

note: Walkway (Hangatahua gorge walk, reached from near Ōkato).

name: Lake Mangamahoe

name: Lake Rotomanu
note: Lake (calm lake at New Plymouth used for wakeboarding), a stop per NZ Pocket Guide only.

name: Lake Rotokare

name: Lake Rotorangi

note: Marine reserve (south Taranaki coast), Wikipedia only.

name: Te Rere o Kapuni

name: East End Beach

name: Mangahume

name: Normanby Dam

name: Ōpunake Beach
